comparator.academicYear: Indicative 2027–2028 year 1, 2028–2029 year 2 and 2029–2030 year 3 prospectus pathway
comparator.sourceNotes: The coherent non-abroad pathway has twelve compulsory 5-EC first-year courses (60 EC). Two 0-EC academic support activities are excluded from the 180-EC total. In year two, six required 5-EC courses total 30 EC, with 30 EC of restricted Faculty of Arts minor choices (two 15-EC minors); additional English language/culture minors are optional rather than required. In year three, the non-abroad pathway consists of four compulsory 5-EC courses, a required 10-EC bachelor thesis in literature or linguistics, and 30 EC of free electives. An abroad version is an alternative study arrangement and is not combined with the domestic version. These year pages are expressly indicative prospectus years and do not establish the final curriculum for a Fall 2026 entrant. Rechecked 13 October 2026: all listed required courses, 30-EC restricted minor space, 30-EC free electives and 10-EC thesis remain supported. The exact named English Language and Culture track is now explicit; the same non-abroad pathway and every component/weight are preserved.

core: Literary interpretation, genres, stylistics and creative expression
High and popular culture, historical society and English-speaking cultural worlds
questions: How cultural narratives represent identity, social relations and historical power

trace: directly teaches practical criticism, fiction, poetry, drama and narrative form, supplying the literary-analysis foundation
directly teaches argument, rhetorical theory and persuasive writing/speaking, contributing to the target communication strand without implying English-proficiency instruction

provides specific complementary modern historical study of industrialisation, sovereignty, war, welfare and decolonisation needed to interpret nineteenth-/twentieth-century cultural works; it is not British history alone
directly studies literary genres, primary texts and their historical themes across Western literary heritage; it is not a dedicated survey of British or American periods
directly analyses linguistic choices and interpretive effects in literary and non-fiction texts through stylistics; it does not supply an English phonology or syntax sequence
directly studies American gender histories through storybooks, interviews, queer cinema and cultural storytelling, contributing a defined cultural-history strand

applies public-speaking, debating and storytelling pedagogy with primary-school children after rhetorical foundations; interaction is principally Dutch, and this is neither secondary-school English teaching nor an English-proficiency course

provides specific complementary comparative study of myth transmission, oral narrative and text-to-image transformations across cultures; it situates English-language literary study within global narrative traditions without claiming English-specific coverage
directly develops film-form and representation analysis to study narratives as cultural production and responses to social change
provides specific complementary study of printed books and pre-digital media as material objects shaping the circulation of knowledge, communication and cultural memory
provides specific complementary theories of race, gender, class and institutions for analysing social relations represented in literature and media
directly studies memoir, autobiography, travel writing and cultural self-representation, including memory and identity in life narratives
directly examines American mainstream media and everyday life from television to TikTok, including storytelling, identity and whose accounts are heard

directly studies Indigenous histories and cultural resistance within the United States through memoir, literature, music, language revival and film; it does not relabel Indigenous culture as English culture
directly analyses documentary histories, genres and the ethical representation of people, with an essay and short documentary production
directly analyses literary adaptation and film form, with documented British-text examples including Pride and Prejudice, Frankenstein and Hamlet; its scope remains wider than English Studies
directly studies race, systemic oppression and cultural representation in American history from the nineteenth century onward, including research-based podcast production
provides specific complementary analysis of imperial power and its historical rise/fall for studying English-speaking cultural worlds; it does not teach the historical spread of English itself
provides specific complementary theories of modernity, imperialism and colonial responses for interpreting cultural narratives and power, rather than generic social breadth
directly applies feminist, Marxist, minority and psychoanalytic approaches in a literary research project
directly studies and practices poetic form, voice, rhythm and performance through critical reading and creative projects
directly investigates the 1809 British Walcheren expedition through diaries, memoirs and official reports, providing a documented British historical subject and primary-source research
provides specific complementary analysis of emotions toward fiction and art and the relationship between aesthetic and moral emotion; this is one interpretive contribution, not the whole programme

alternatives.label: Literature, rhetoric & cultural history
alternatives.concept: Study literary form, stylistics, rhetoric and film alongside American cultural representation and source-based modern history. Social theory and the philosophy of emotion support specific analyses of identity, power and responses to fiction; English phonology, syntax, proficiency training and the full British literary-period sequence remain gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: Six literature courses, four communication courses, five media courses and five history courses dominate; two sociology courses and one philosophy course provide explicitly traced complementary methods. The label describes the completed related-fields composition and does not promise an English Language and Culture degree.
progression: All exact workbook terms and formal prerequisites pass. Literary introduction and stylistics precede advanced literary research; rhetoric precedes its practice module; film introduction precedes documentary and adaptation; introductory sociology precedes Modern Sociology; modern history precedes the source-based seminar. Level-three Philosophy of Emotion has no formal prerequisite and is placed in the final semester.

candidates.label: English structural, historical and global linguistics
Advanced English proficiency and language development
English in science, politics and business

selection.assessment: One complete related-fields response is defensible. The literature/culture specialization is substantively covered by that curriculum and does not establish a second distinct direction. The first proposed additional direction, English structural/historical/global linguistics, lacks a cumulative language-specific sequence: stylistics and Psycholinguistics provide limited contributions, not phonology, syntax, historical linguistics or world-English sociolinguistics. Advanced proficiency also lacks a dedicated development sequence. English being used in science, politics and business does not evidence a coherent independent curriculum in those three fields. Teaching was assessed through Rhetoric in Action, Psycholinguistics, brain/behaviour foundations and lifespan development: these do not establish a complete English-learning/secondary pedagogy curriculum. Its rejection concerns academic content, not professional qualification alone. Stop at one; no third alternative is attempted.

notes.text: Radboud combines English proficiency, linguistics and sustained British/American literary study with independent research. This UCR programme approaches literary and cultural questions through literature, rhetoric, media and history. It provides related fields rather than the full English Language and Culture curriculum: dedicated English proficiency, phonetics, phonology, syntax and historical-English study are absent, and its British literary-period coverage is less extensive.
